claims.statement: UNESCO places the northern Japanese sequence represented by these sites at approximately 13,000–400 BCE.
Settled communities relied on hunting, fishing and gathering; their sites preserve dwellings, graves, earthworks and stone circles.

evidence.note: Regional archaeological context for southern Hokkaido and northern Tohoku. Dates do not apply uniformly to all Japan or every settlement. The full sequence begins before the initial study window. No single map point represents these scattered sites.
